newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-JUVENTUS THRASH AJAX TO REACH EUROPEAN FINAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-JUVENTUS THRASH AJAX TO REACH EUROPEAN FINAL.

text.p: Champions Juventus demolished former winners Ajax Amsterdam 4-1 and 6-2 on aggregate on Wednesday to celebrate their club centenary year with a fifth European Cup final.
After drawing 1-1 and then beating the Dutch team on penalties in last year's final in Rome, Juventus showed Ajax what they were really capable of in Turin.
They now meet Germany's Borussia Dortmund, the last team to beat them in Europe, in the final in Munich.
Attilio Lombardo opened the scoring in the 34th minute and Christian Vieri made it 2-0 in the 36th.
Lombardo headed in off a corner from French midfielder Zinedine Zidane and Italy international Vieri hit a volley at the far post off a cross from Lombardo.
Both goals were completely against the run of play with Ajax tearing through the Juventus defence in the opening 20 minutes but failing to find the net.
Zidane was also behind the other two goals, setting up Nicola Amoruso in the 80th after doing all the hard work and then passing for a simple tap-in.
He then scored a virtuoso goal in the 82nd as the fans chanted his name and that of coach Marcello Lippi.
The defeat ended Ajax's proud unbeaten away record in Europe since 1994 and kept Juve on course for a third title and a remarkable treble.

Only Internazionale, who reached the UEFA Cup final on Tuesday by beating Monaco, have previously won the Italian league title, the European Cup and the world club cup in the same season. They achieved the feat in 1964-65.
Juventus are already the world club champions and have a six-point lead at the top of serie A.
